response.title: Will a battery power station run a gas tankless water heater so we still have hot showers when the power is out?
response.answer:
Yes! A portable battery power station can run most gas tankless water heaters during a power outage, allowing you to continue taking hot showers.

In fact, gas tankless water heaters are excellent candidates for battery backup because natural gas does the actual water heating, while electricity only powers the electronics and supporting components.

How much electricity does a gas tankless water heater need?

A typical residential gas tankless water heater uses electricity for:

Electronic ignition

Control board and temperature sensors

Combustion and exhaust fans

Internal freeze-protection heaters (on some models)

Typical power requirements:

Operating condition

	

Approximate power




Standby

	

2–10 watts




Heating water for a shower

	

40–150 watts




Startup or certain operating conditions

	

150–300+ watts




Freeze protection

	

Varies significantly

Actual consumption depends on the model.

How long could a battery run it?

Assuming your heater draws 80 watts while running and 5 watts on standby, with 85% usable battery efficiency:

Battery capacity

	

Approximate backup runtime*




300 Wh

	

3 hours




500 Wh

	

5 hours




1,000 Wh

	

10 hours




2,000 Wh

	

21 hours

These are estimates for continuous heater operation, not how long the battery lasts with occasional showers.

For example, a 1,000 Wh battery could theoretically support dozens of 10-minute showers over several days, assuming normal standby consumption and no other significant loads.

What kind of power station should you use?

For a typical gas tankless heater, I'd look for:

Pure sine wave AC output, 120V.

At least 500W continuous AC output, subject to your heater's actual specifications.

500–1,000 Wh battery capacity for a useful emergency reserve.

UPS/EPS functionality if you want automatic backup when utility power fails.

Proper grounding and electrical compatibility with the heater.

Rinnai, for example, explicitly supports battery backup for certain models and documents tested backup runtimes. 
Rinnai
+1

One important caution: some tankless heaters require a properly grounded dedicated connection and prohibit extension cords. If yours is hardwired, have an electrician install an approved backup arrangement rather than improvising a connection. 
Rinnai

Also, the gas supply and water pressure must remain available. Homes using an electric well pump or booster pump may need backup power for that equipment too.

I can help you size one for your exact heater

Two questions:

What brand and model is your gas tankless water heater? (Rinnai, Navien, Rheem, Noritz, etc.)

How long do you want hot water during an outage? One day, three days, or longer?

With those details, I can estimate the battery capacity needed and whether a relatively small power station will be sufficient.
